game.title: Moon Mission (Abbie's World, AW-STUDY-0036)
platforms: Mac or PC browser on a big TV

core.fantasy: A family flies a pink rocket to the Moon together on the living-room TV: each person has an important job, everyone votes on the story, and launch control talks back for real.
pillars: Everyone has a job, and the mission can't go on without it
We decide together (vote, and the Captain's Hat breaks ties)
Launch control is a real voice you talk to
A real-feeling launch day, felt as a six-year-old
Nothing fails; mistakes are shared and funny
core.signature_moment: Abbie yells "PLUG IN OUR OXYGEN!!!", slaps her key, the hose clicks in and the green light comes on, and Houston answers "Oxygen is GO" a heartbeat before the countdown starts.
anti_goals: no fail screens or blaming one child
no reading required: every line is also spoken
no HUD in play; panels, paper and voices carry the information
no copied story, characters, ship designs or music from any reference game

signatures.description: Each beat gives each person a named job on their own key; the beat waits for its owner, and a stalled job can be helped.
Houston is a real-time voice on a push-to-talk radio that runs a fixed launch script and improvises around it.
Group choices are `> ` lines with a coloured vote chip per person; ties go to whoever wears the Captain's Hat, which moves every choice.
First person with your own gloved hands; Earth is light mode (white suits, daylight), the Moon is dark mode (black sky, glowing trim), and the launch is the switch between them.
The capsule panel on screen matches a real key panel on the coffee table, picture for picture.
A real mission clock counts down to launch from the first scene, shown on things and on film-style mission cards, with planned holds so nobody fails.

audience.age: two six-year-olds with a parent (2-4 players)
audience.skill_floor: press your one key; shouting helps
audience.context: big TV after ballet, one evening per act

verbs.input: tap a character, pick a topic

steps: choices change later lines and items
memory key or coin at the end of each act

rules.scoring: points for gentle landings and helping hands, shown on things

systems: one launch signal driving light, shake, sound and music

emergent_behaviours: kids shouting jobs at each other

controls_count.method: per child: their job key and RADIO

art.direction: Light mode on Earth, dark mode on the Moon: Faceted Hero characters in white suits with colour trim, the pink rocket in nearly every shot, tactile picture-labelled panels, one crisp mission-card layer
reference_style_only: Deliver Us Mars opening (rhythm: quiet home, tactile cockpit, voice in your ear, roar, silence)

information_grammar.principle: Panels, paper checklists, job glows on keys and seats, and voices; captions with > choices are the only words.

pacing.session: 30-45 minutes per act, ending somewhere cosy
pacing.transitions: a calm 8-15 s cutscene between every scene, with the mission card

style: first-person tactile launch day (from the Deliver Us Mars opening's rhythm)
real launch-control callouts in kid words
expression: Deliver Us Mars's story, characters, ship and music are never copied; the rocket, cast, script and music are ours
